papers.title: Hybrid additive manufacturing of Inconel 718 for future space applications
papers.abstract: We present a detailed analysis of the hybrid fabrication of test parts made from Inconel 718 using two additive-manufacturing (AM) technologies: selective laser melting (SLM) and directed-energy deposition (DED). This combination should allow the manufacturing of larger parts with geometrically complex structures that no other technologies could achieve. However, it is necessary to ensure the consistency of the mechanical properties of such parts. The hybrid SLM/DED parts, as well as the individual SLM and DED processed parts, were evaluated in terms of microstructures and mechanical properties, to understand the mechanisms that control the properties. We introduced a custom solution treatment and aging to dissolve the Laves phase, which was present in the DED part, where it reduced the mechanical properties. For a hybrid part with excellent properties, there must be good bonding between the SLM and DED parts, while the DED process must be adapted to prevent δ-phase precipitation. This new technology has the potential to produce high-added-value metallic products for space applications, that benefit from the properties developed through hybrid AM.

summary_en.motivation: To develop hybrid additively manufactured Inconel 718 parts for space applications.
summary_en.method: Combined selective laser melting and directed energy deposition with custom solution treatment and aging.
summary_en.result: Hybrid parts achieved good properties but required careful process control to avoid δ-phase precipitation.

papers.title: Minimally invasive maxillary sinus augmentation with simultaneous implantation on an elderly patient: A case report.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: In this case study, a minimally invasive transalveolar approach using platelet-rich fibrin and bone substitute with simultaneous implantation was carried out in an elderly patient. We analyzed the cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) findings to evaluate bone regeneration. CASE SUMMARY: A 65-year-old female with no contraindications for dental implants and loss of maxillary bilateral molars is described. Examination by CBCT showed the available vertical bone height in the bilateral posterior maxilla was 0.5-6.8 mm in the left and 2.8-6.5 mm in the right. The patient underwent a transalveolar approach using platelet-rich fibrin and bone substitute with simulataneous placement of an implant 10 mm in length. Six months post-surgery, the implant showed excellent osseointegration with the bone graft. Thereafter, full-ceramic crowns were fitted. Follow-up at 2 years demonstrated satisfactory prognosis. CONCLUSION: Platelet-rich fibrin and bone substitute can be used to augment the maxillary sinus with a vertical bone height less than 4 mm.

llm.relevance_to_user: 此论文为临床病例报告，完全不涉及增材制造、力学测试或生物力学研究。
llm.why_not_core: This paper is a clinical case report on sinus augmentation surgery with no LPBF fabrication, mechanical testing, fatigue analysis, or implant biomechanics. It does not address porous structure, stress shielding, or osseointegration in the context of AM biomedical materials.

summary_zh.motivation: 老年患者上颌窦提升及同期种植的微创方法探讨
summary_zh.method: 采用富血小板纤维蛋白和骨替代材料经牙槽突入路提升上颌窦并同期植入种植体
summary_zh.result: 2年随访显示种植体骨结合良好，预后满意
summary_zh.validation: CBCT评估骨再生及临床随访

summary_en.motivation: To investigate a minimally invasive transalveolar sinus augmentation technique combined with simultaneous implant placement in an elderly patient with insufficient bone height.
summary_en.method: Platelet-rich fibrin and bone substitute were used via a transalveolar approach, and a 10-mm implant was placed simultaneously, with bone regeneration evaluated by CBCT.
summary_en.result: At 6 months, the implant showed excellent osseointegration with the graft, and 2-year follow-up indicated satisfactory prognosis.
summary_en.validation: Clinical follow-up and CBCT imaging were used to assess bone regeneration and implant stability.
